title: Membership of the SPS2 agent-name token set is ungoverned: 'antigravity' and 'autonomous' require a User decision
authority_note: SUPERSEDED. This record REQUESTED a decision; it never granted one and never claimed to. All token-set decisions now live in ATTRIBUTION-POLICY-DECISIONS.json.

problem.summary: No approved requirement, decision, evidence record or schema has ever enumerated which words count as agent names. The token set is an implementation heuristic that SPEC-2 consolidated wholesale, not a set adopted through a membership decision. The same rule this file relies on - that additions AND removals are governed changes - therefore applies to SPEC-2's own removals, which remain unratified.

governing_requirements_are_generic.REQ-P5-03: 'An approval must be attributable to an identifiable User' / 'An agent-attributed approval must be rejected' - names no token
governing_requirements_are_generic.REQ-P5-04: 'The agent-attribution detector lives in governance, not core' - governs PLACEMENT only, not membership
governing_requirements_are_generic.schema_text: sps2/governance/SCHEMAS/decision.schema.json and capability.schema.json say approval 'MUST NOT name an agent, model or automation' - categories, not tokens

problem.negative_evidence: Searched sps2/decisions, sps2/requirements, sps2/evidence, sps2/handoff, sps2/schemas, sps2/governance and .sps/architecture for 'antigravity'. The only hits are the two files this investigation created: sps2/governance/attribution_policy.json and sps2/decisions/OPEN-DECISION-ATTRIBUTION-TOKEN-SET.json. `git log -S antigravity -- sps2/decisions sps2/requirements sps2/evidence sps2/handoff` returns empty. No approved requirement, decision, evidence record, schema, handoff or architecture document names 'antigravity' as an agent-name token.
problem.canonical_set_provenance_is_equally_weak: 'aider' and 'windsurf' appear in no requirement, decision, evidence record or schema either. They are present only in the three core-neutrality vendor lists (sps2/tools/validate-p5.py, sps2/tools/test-portability.py, sps2/tests/test_p5.py) which attribution_policy.json itself classes as a DIFFERENT vocabulary answering a different question. All 16 tokens landed complete in sps2/governance/attribution.py at commit 593188a with no membership decision. There is therefore no principled basis on which the canonical 16 outrank any other validator's list.

open_questions.question: Should 'antigravity' be admitted to the canonical agent-name token set?
open_questions.classification: UNDECIDED - not an accidental regression, and not a settled exclusion
evidence_that_it_was_ever_a_policy_token: sps2/tools/check_sps2.py at commit 94d23e1 (2026-10-03) listed it in an APPROVER denylist that judged approval.decided_by and global_installation_authorized_by. An approval attributed to 'Antigravity' was rejected before consolidation and is not rejected now.

sps2/tools/validate-sps2.sh:189 lists it beside claude, cursor, codex, gemini, opencode and cline, six of which ARE canonical tokens. NOTE this is the core-neutrality BRAND scan, which attribution_policy.json classes as a DIFFERENT vocabulary that must not be merged; it is cited here only as evidence that the project treats antigravity as a vendor peer of the canonical tokens, NOT as evidence of policy membership.
evidence_that_it_is_not_governed: No approved requirement, decision, evidence record or schema names it.
The commit that introduced it (94d23e1) has an empty commit body and records no rationale.
The three core-neutrality vendor lists do NOT contain it, so the project's vendor vocabulary was never uniform.
open_questions.why_it_is_not_a_typo: Antigravity is a first-class, actively supported agent host in this repository: skills/sps/hosts/antigravity.md, skills/sps-cms/hosts/antigravity.md, skills/sps-cms/package.json, install.sh --agent antigravity, and .sps/architecture/SPS2-AGENT-INTEROPERABILITY.md which rates Gemini/Antigravity HIGH risk. An approval attributed to it is a plausible value.
open_questions.current_effect: Latent, not active. No record in the repository carries 'Antigravity' as a decided_by / approved_by / authorised_by value, so nothing currently changes verdict.

options.option: A. Admit 'antigravity' to the canonical token set
options.consequence: Restores check_sps2.py's pre-consolidation detection. Rejects an approver named 'Antigravity', 'antigravity' or 'antigravity-cli'. Does NOT create a false positive on any human surname.
options.risk: None identified. It is a proper noun for an agent host, not an ordinary English word.

options.option: B. Leave it excluded and accept the gap
options.consequence: Keeps the canonical 16 stable. An approval attributed to Antigravity is accepted by every validator.
options.risk: Silently contradicts REQ-P5-03's 'an agent-attributed approval must be rejected' for a vendor this repository actively supports.

open_questions.recommendation: Option A. The evidence that it is a real agent outweighs the absence of a membership decision; and because no approved text forbids it, admitting it changes no approved criterion. This recommendation is NOT implemented - it needs a User decision.
open_questions.current_policy_behaviour: ADMITTED - member of tokens[] per DEC-0025
open_questions.resolution: ANTIGRAVITY ADMITTED to the canonical token set. The recommendation (Option A) was accepted.

open_questions.question: Should 'autonomous' remain excluded from the canonical token set?
open_questions.resolution: KEPT EXCLUDED. No directly applicable approved requirement made admission possible or necessary.

secondary_finding.statement: sps2/governance/attribution_policy.json states that adding OR REMOVING a token is 'a governed change requiring a User decision record'. No such record exists for the SPEC-2 consolidation itself: the whole policy file is untracked and there is no SPEC-2 task record or decision record anywhere in the repository. The consolidation is self-documented only by the policy file's own comments and two test suites.
secondary_finding.implication: Future token changes have no governance anchor. Closing this would mean creating a decision record that ratifies the canonical 16 as the approved set - which is itself a User decision and is NOT taken here.

advisory_assessment_not_a_ratification.$comment: Retained for provenance. Both assessments were ADVISORY and have since been superseded by DEC-0027 (self, script) and DEC-0026 (autonomous), which recorded the User's formal decision.
advisory_assessment_not_a_ratification.finding: No approved requirement, decision, evidence record or schema names either token in either direction. At HEAD each appeared in 3 of the 10 pre-consolidation shell approver-token sites (validate-p3.sh:206, validate-p4.sh:246, validate-p4.sh:459) and in NONE of the 5 hardcoded Python denylists. Admitting them would reject ordinary human surnames such as 'Jane Self', 'Marcus Self', 'Nora Script' and 'Mr Script'.
advisory_assessment_not_a_ratification.outcome: RATIFIED as excluded by DEC-0027 on 2026-10-15.

supersession_note: Every question in this record has been resolved by an explicit User decision recorded in sps2/decisions/ATTRIBUTION-POLICY-DECISIONS.json. This record is RETAINED, not deleted, because it documents the evidence that informed those decisions. It is no longer the live statement of the policy's status. Note for readers: this file's decision_id and envelope never matched the sps2/decision/v1 convention (id must match ^DEC-[0-9]{4}$ inside a decisions[] array), so check_sps2.py inspected it vacuously and reported success without examining anything. The replacement record is conformant and is genuinely validated.
